top.title: Kimi Antonelli explains mistake that left him “smoked by the two McLarens” in Vegas
top.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli looked primed to cap a charge from sixth on the grid with a dramatic last-lap victory at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Instead, one split-second pedal adjustment drained his battery dry - handing Max Verstappen breathing room and dropping the Mercedes driver off the podium entirely. After topping Friday qualifying before a five-place power unit penalty relegated him to sixth, Antonelli used an alternative medium-to-soft tyre strategy to slice back into contention. When team-mate George Russell locked up into the Turn 5 barrier late in the race, Antonelli stood as Verstappen’s lone remaining threat. Yet heading onto the final lap, his W17 abruptly slowed exiting the final chicane, allowing Lando Norris (+0.639 seconds) and Oscar Piastri (+1.529s from 17th on the grid) to sweep past into Turn 1. Antonelli crossed the line fourth, 2.574s behind Verstappen and just 0.353s ahead of Alpine ’s Pierre Gasly . Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Speaking afterwards to Sky Sports F1’s Craig Slater, Antonelli clarified that switching his energy deployment map was not to blame - his attempt to manage the gap behind Verstappen disrupted the car's regeneration cycle. "No, I think the change of deployment was good because it was the best option to then stay ahead after the chicane in case I was overtaking Max before Turn 14," Antonelli explained. "But because I wanted to keep the overtake mode, I lift off and reapply some throttle to keep a little bit of speed, and that messed up the whole battery harvesting, and I stayed in the chicane at zero. "So I lost more than a second going into Turn 1, and not only I couldn't stay close to Max and give myself a good shot for the win, but I got smoked by the two McLarens as well and lost the podium," he added. "So probably it was a mistake on my side, but in the moment it's also very difficult because I thought I was doing something right to stay behind and keep the overtake." High-speed chess match with Verstappen The error carried an ironic twist after Antonelli spent Thursday praising Mercedes as likely the grid’s most efficient package in electrical energy management heading into power-sensitive Nevada. Across the final 15 laps, however, neither Mercedes nor Red Bull wanted to lead too early down the 1.9-kilometre Strip straight, triggering a tense game of cat and mouse over overtake mode. "I didn't force anything, and I was just trying to stay behind, keep the overtake to give myself the best shot at the end, especially for the last two straights." top.title: Fred Vasseur "more than upset" with "unacceptable" Lewis Hamilton-Charles Leclerc Las Vegas clash
top.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari Formula 1 team principal Fred Vasseur said that Charles Leclerc's clash with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "completely unacceptable", and added he was "more than upset" that the team's message to its drivers seems to have been ignored again. Leclerc spun Hamilton around while the team-mates fought over sixth place around the streets of Las Vegas. Hamilton dropped to 10th and recovered to finish seventh , while Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty and finished 10th. Speaking to Sky Sports after the race, Vasseur said the team had repeated the message it gave after Mexico. "Clearly, it's unacceptable. First, a little bit the same message as Mexico, because you have to think about the team, about the people working in Maranello, about all the stakeholders, the sponsors," he said. The team chief revealed Ferrari had spoken to Leclerc during the race, explaining that the nature of the Las Vegas track meant its drivers had to focus on the cars around them. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake, because in this kind of race, as you were saying before, you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you are passed by the others. It means that you have to do your race," he continued. "And Charles, it's clearly a mistake that is penalising the team a lot. And it's completely unacceptable today. Honestly, I'm more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico." The pair clashed on the opening lap in Mexico three weeks ago, when Leclerc was given a five-second penalty for passing Hamilton off the track. Ferrari then held talks with both drivers. "We had a chat together, all together, in Brazil. Today we passed the message to think about the team when they were racing together. And the outcome is this one," Vasseur said. "It's mega frustrating for all of us." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

top.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
top.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps, Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. top.title: Lewis Hamilton: Las Vegas penalty "really harsh" as podium chance slipped
top.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton says his 10-second penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "really harsh" as his chance of a podium slipped from his fingers during a chaotic race. Hamilton started 11th after both Ferraris were knocked out in Q2. He climbed quickly through the field, but was penalised for leaving the track and gaining an advantage at the Turn 7-8 chicane while battling McLaren's Lando Norris . He then lost even more of the ground he'd made up when team-mate Charles Leclerc spun him around while they fought over sixth, dropping him to 10th. Hamilton fought back to finish seventh, while Leclerc was penalised and finished 10th. "We knew that we were faced with massive challenges this weekend. We didn't realise there would be such a limitation on the straights," Hamilton told Sky Sports. "The qualifying, obviously, was difficult, but in the race I felt great, and I really was progressing well." He didn't hide how he felt about the penalty. "Then avoiding collision with one of the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty, which was, I think, really harsh, which was frustrating. But I just got my head back down and just kept chasing and managed to get back in the fight," he said. "Then again, I got knocked back again. But I never gave up, and I was just trying to get the best results. I really think we could have had a podium today." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Hamilton didn't hide his feelings during the race, either. In a message not broadcast on the world feed , he hinted at the five-second penalty Leclerc was given for a similar off-track pass in Mexico, saying: "They give me 10 for avoiding an incident." Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur agreed the punishment was too harsh, saying: "Honestly, I was surprised with the 10 seconds." Hamilton would not be drawn on the collision with Leclerc, saying it was "something for you to speak to Ferrari about". Asked whether it was time for proper rules between the two Ferrari drivers after Mexico, he said: "I've done all I can, and I've said everything and more." "All I can do is just show up and give it everything I can, and hopefully in the background they'll eventually figure it out." The result moves Hamilton up to third in the drivers' standings on 267 points, three ahead of George Russell and Lando Norris, with two races to go. top.title: Messi Tops 2026 MLS Salary List at $28.3M, Lewandowski Jumps to No. 2
top.description: Messi Tops 2026 MLS Salary List at $28.3M, Lewandowski Jumps to No. 2 Lionel Messi remains Major League Soccer's highest-paid player, with $28.3 million in guaranteed compensation for 2026, according to the MLS Players Association's final salary release of the year. Robert Lewandowski, who joined Chicago Fire in June, has overtaken Son Heung-min for second place at $19.51 million. The gap at the top is still enormous. Messi's guaranteed pay is up from $20.45 million a year ago, and his individual number now runs more than double the entire Philadelphia Union roster , which carries the league's lowest total payroll at $12.64 million. Why Messi's number keeps climbing Messi signed a contract extension through the 2028 season last fall, and the new MLSPA figures reflect that deal's structure rather than a fresh negotiation. His $25 million base salary plus bonuses produces the $28.3 million guaranteed figure — and that's before factoring in revenue-sharing from Apple's MLS Season Pass and sponsorship income that Inter Miami co-owner Jorge Mas has said pushes his real annual take closer to $70-80 million. Lewandowski's arrival tells a parallel story about where MLS spending is headed. His $16 million base salary and $19.51 million guaranteed compensation make him the clearest marker yet that clubs outside Miami are now willing to commit Designated Player money at a scale that was rare even two years ago. Under MLS's salary budget rules, each Designated Player's actual salary can run far above the roster cap — only a fixed charge, $803,125 for players 24 and older, counts against a club's budget, with the team absorbing the rest. That mechanism, not the cap itself, is what makes both Messi's and Lewandowski's deals possible. What it means for the league's financial pecking order The broader numbers back up the sense that MLS wages are moving, not just at the top. Total guaranteed compensation across the league reached $724.5 million, up nearly 15% from the May release, and 150 players are now earning at least $1 million annually. Average guaranteed compensation sits at $746,936, an 18% jump year over year. Still, the hierarchy hasn't flattened — it's stretched. Lewandowski, Antoine Griezmann, Son and Breel Embolo round out a five-player tier earning $10 million or more, but Messi sits well clear of all of them. Inter Miami's roster spending now tops the league, and the club's willingness to build around one player's market value continues to set the ceiling other front offices are chasing rather than matching. As more marquee strikers arrive mid-contract-cycle — as Lewandowski did — expect the gap between MLS's top tier and its median roster to keep widening before it narrows.

top.title: Man United’s trip to Sporting: Paulo Fonseca explains how he is preparing for Champions League tie
top.description: Man United’s trip to Sporting: Paulo Fonseca explains how he is preparing for Champions League tie Manchester United kick off the Mauricio Pochettino era with a blockbuster game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, 22 November, in the Premier League. The Red Devils are 18th in the Premier League after 10 games this season and have registered just one win in the league. The Argentine , as such, has a mini challenge at hand as he attempts to get a faltering side firing on all cylinders. Pochettino will have to make do with the options at hand until at least the January transfer window, when he could have the chance to seek squad improvements. The 54-year-old is facing a daunting task, as the team is set to play 11 times in 34 days starting on Sunday. Immediately after the Liverpool match is a trip to Portugal to face Sporting CP in the Champions League. Pochettino will be eyeing a long run in Europe United returned to the Champions League this season following a two-year absence. However, their run in Europe has hardly been convincing. The Red Devils started well, securing a 4-0 win over Sabah on Matchday One, which remains their only clean sheet across competitions this season. However, the English giants succumbed to a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Atlético Madrid next. Things went from bad to worse in their third game in Europe’s premier club competition, with Como thrashing them 4-1. That also prompted Bruno Fernandes to publicly question former manager Michael Carrick’s tactics. United looked set for another disaster in the game against AS Roma, in which they were 2-0 behind by the 17th minute. However, the English giants fought back to secure a 3-2 win to keep hopes alive of progressing to the knockouts. The English giants are currently 17th in the table, with the top eight securing automatic qualification to the next stage, while teams from ninth to 24th have to go through play-offs. A win against Sporting next week could massively help their cause, but the Portuguese club have already begun preparations for the tie. Manchester United Champions League Results: 2026/27 Season Paulo Fonseca to watch United game against Liverpool Speaking after Saturday’s 4-0 win over União da Serra, as cited by A Bola , Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca revealed that he will keep a close watch on how United perform under Pochettino this weekend. top.description: Dynamo Kyiv 1999 GFX - Getty/GOAL No Ukrainian side has ever side won the European Cup - but Valeriy Lobanovskyi's wonderful side went close in 1999 When Valeriy Lobanovskyi faced the media after Dynamo Kyiv's Champions League semi-final second-leg loss to Bayern Munich at the Olympic Stadium in April 1999, he insisted that elimination was "no tragedy". "We are happy to have made it to the last four," he said. However, Andriy Shevchenko and the rest of his team-mates were devastated - and more for their coach than the club, the supporters or even themselves. "I hated seeing the expression on Lobanovskyi's face," the striker later wrote in his autobiography . "I could see how much he had wanted to win that trophy." And Dynamo really should have done. While everyone remembers that Bayern should have gone to beat Manchester United in the final because the nature of their injury-time collapse at Camp Nou was so unforgettable, it's often overlooked that the Bavarians were blessed to have even made it to Barcelona. Dynamo had Bayern on the ropes in the first leg of their semi in Kyiv and Lobanovskyi's wonderful side would have arguably caused Sir Alex Ferguson's United even more problems in Catalunya. After all, the Ukrainian underdogs had spent the previous two seasons upsetting Europe's elite. 'On the trail of perfection' Lobanovskyi is essentially one of the founding fathers of modern football For one of the most influential figures in football history, Lobanovskyi's name is not as well-known as it should be. The modern game simply would not be what it is today without the Ukrainian, who was very much a pioneer in terms of the use of scientific data to analyse matches and opponents. The importance he attached to team work and peak physical condition is also the stuff of legend, with Shevchenko claiming to have seen team-mates begging the coach to call off particularly punishing training sessions. He never did, though. "He was a genius," Shevchenko said , "a visionary and a subversive, perpetually on the trail of perfection." Given Lobanovskyi was also a master of psychology, players were willing to run through walls for him - which is why he managed to build two great Dynamo teams, a decade apart, in the 1970s and 80s. top.title: Troops raid bandits’ hideout in Kogi, recover AK-47 rifles
top.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation. The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targeted suspected kidnappers operating in the Osara, Gada and Ohakiti forest areas of Okehi Local Government Area, following intelligence reports on their activities and hideouts. In a statement, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the operation was launched by troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba in collaboration with other security personnel. She said the operation was aimed at dismantling criminal hideouts linked to the recent spate of kidnappings along the Kabba–Okene Road and neighbouring communities. According to the statement, troops encountered about six armed bandits at an abandoned settlement within the forest during the offensive, engaging them and forcing them to flee. A subsequent search of the hideout led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered from the enclave included bags, torchlights, food supplies and a power bank believed to have been used by the fleeing suspects. The Army said the operation underscored its determination to deny criminal elements freedom of action, dismantle their operational bases and restore security along vulnerable routes and communities in Kogi State. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property. The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to identify and clear hideouts used by criminal elements across the country. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation. The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targeted suspected kidnappers operating in the Osara, Gada and Ohakiti forest areas of Okehi Local Government Area, following intelligence reports on their activities and hideouts. In a statement, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the operation was launched by troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba in collaboration with other security personnel. She said the operation was aimed at dismantling criminal hideouts linked to the recent spate of kidnappings along the Kabba–Okene Road and neighbouring communities. According to the statement, troops encountered about six armed bandits at an abandoned settlement within the forest during the offensive, engaging them and forcing them to flee. A subsequent search of the hideout led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered from the enclave included bags, torchlights, food supplies and a power bank believed to have been used by the fleeing suspects. The Army said the operation underscored its determination to deny criminal elements freedom of action, dismantle their operational bases and restore security along vulnerable routes and communities in Kogi State. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property. The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to identify and clear hideouts used by criminal elements across the country. nigeria.title: Otti disowns viral statement against campaign rallies, calls it fake
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has disowned a viral social media statement purportedly credited to him, describing it as fake and warning the public against spreading misinformation. The statement, which circulated on X (formerly Twitter), quoted Otti as saying that incumbent governors who embark on campaigns have no business doing so if they have performed well, arguing that their achievements should speak for them and secure their re-election. It also quoted the governor as saying he was not campaigning and that Abia residents should re-elect him only if they considered his performance satisfactory. However, the governor, through his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, on Friday, dismissed the statement and the X account that published it as fake. Ekeoma, who signed the disclaimer, said Otti never made the statement and urged the public not to be misled by the publication. He explained that, contrary to the impression created by the viral post, the governor was already campaigning and had been touring different parts of the state to interact with voters and obtain firsthand feedback, particularly from grassroots communities. According to him, Otti considers campaigns a legitimate component of the electoral process and could not have disparaged politicians for engaging in them. “The Governor believes that campaigns are legitimate parts of the electoral process and thus could not have dismissed it or cast aspersions on those campaigning,” Ekeoma said. The state government urged members of the public to disregard the purported statement and the account responsible for circulating it, while calling on those behind the publication to immediately take it down and desist from misrepresenting the governor. It also cautioned individuals using Otti’s popularity to generate online traffic to ensure that information published in his name is truthful, warning that deliberate misrepresentation could attract the attention of law enforcement agencies. The disclaimer comes amid growing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, with social media increasingly serving as a platform for political messaging, claims and counterclaims. Meanwhile, Vanguard investigations indicate that Otti currently faces no formidable challenger in the forthcoming governorship election. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported. Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600. Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record. Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. sports.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli looked primed to cap a charge from sixth on the grid with a dramatic last-lap victory at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Instead, one split-second pedal adjustment drained his battery dry - handing Max Verstappen breathing room and dropping the Mercedes driver off the podium entirely. After topping Friday qualifying before a five-place power unit penalty relegated him to sixth, Antonelli used an alternative medium-to-soft tyre strategy to slice back into contention. When team-mate George Russell locked up into the Turn 5 barrier late in the race, Antonelli stood as Verstappen’s lone remaining threat. Yet heading onto the final lap, his W17 abruptly slowed exiting the final chicane, allowing Lando Norris (+0.639 seconds) and Oscar Piastri (+1.529s from 17th on the grid) to sweep past into Turn 1. Antonelli crossed the line fourth, 2.574s behind Verstappen and just 0.353s ahead of Alpine ’s Pierre Gasly . "No, I think the change of deployment was good because it was the best option to then stay ahead after the chicane in case I was overtaking Max before Turn 14," Antonelli explained. "But because I wanted to keep the overtake mode, I lift off and reapply some throttle to keep a little bit of speed, and that messed up the whole battery harvesting, and I stayed in the chicane at zero. "So I lost more than a second going into Turn 1, and not only I couldn't stay close to Max and give myself a good shot for the win, but I got smoked by the two McLarens as well and lost the podium," he added. sports.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
sports.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps, Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. sports.title: Messi Tops 2026 MLS Salary List at $28.3M, Lewandowski Jumps to No. 2
sports.description: Messi Tops 2026 MLS Salary List at $28.3M, Lewandowski Jumps to No. 2 Lionel Messi remains Major League Soccer's highest-paid player, with $28.3 million in guaranteed compensation for 2026, according to the MLS Players Association's final salary release of the year. Robert Lewandowski, who joined Chicago Fire in June, has overtaken Son Heung-min for second place at $19.51 million. The gap at the top is still enormous. Messi's guaranteed pay is up from $20.45 million a year ago, and his individual number now runs more than double the entire Philadelphia Union roster , which carries the league's lowest total payroll at $12.64 million. Why Messi's number keeps climbing Messi signed a contract extension through the 2028 season last fall, and the new MLSPA figures reflect that deal's structure rather than a fresh negotiation. His $25 million base salary plus bonuses produces the $28.3 million guaranteed figure — and that's before factoring in revenue-sharing from Apple's MLS Season Pass and sponsorship income that Inter Miami co-owner Jorge Mas has said pushes his real annual take closer to $70-80 million. Lewandowski's arrival tells a parallel story about where MLS spending is headed. His $16 million base salary and $19.51 million guaranteed compensation make him the clearest marker yet that clubs outside Miami are now willing to commit Designated Player money at a scale that was rare even two years ago. Under MLS's salary budget rules, each Designated Player's actual salary can run far above the roster cap — only a fixed charge, $803,125 for players 24 and older, counts against a club's budget, with the team absorbing the rest. That mechanism, not the cap itself, is what makes both Messi's and Lewandowski's deals possible. What it means for the league's financial pecking order The broader numbers back up the sense that MLS wages are moving, not just at the top. Total guaranteed compensation across the league reached $724.5 million, up nearly 15% from the May release, and 150 players are now earning at least $1 million annually. Average guaranteed compensation sits at $746,936, an 18% jump year over year. Still, the hierarchy hasn't flattened — it's stretched. Lewandowski, Antoine Griezmann, Son and Breel Embolo round out a five-player tier earning $10 million or more, but Messi sits well clear of all of them. Inter Miami's roster spending now tops the league, and the club's willingness to build around one player's market value continues to set the ceiling other front offices are chasing rather than matching. As more marquee strikers arrive mid-contract-cycle — as Lewandowski did — expect the gap between MLS's top tier and its median roster to keep widening before it narrows.

"We are happy to have made it to the last four," he said. However, Andriy Shevchenko and the rest of his team-mates were devastated - and more for their coach than the club, the supporters or even themselves. "I hated seeing the expression on Lobanovskyi's face," the striker later wrote in his autobiography . "I could see how much he had wanted to win that trophy." And Dynamo really should have done. While everyone remembers that Bayern should have gone to beat Manchester United in the final because the nature of their injury-time collapse at Camp Nou was so unforgettable, it's often overlooked that the Bavarians were blessed to have even made it to Barcelona. Dynamo had Bayern on the ropes in the first leg of their semi in Kyiv and Lobanovskyi's wonderful side would have arguably caused Sir Alex Ferguson's United even more problems in Catalunya. After all, the Ukrainian underdogs had spent the previous two seasons upsetting Europe's elite. 'On the trail of perfection' Lobanovskyi is essentially one of the founding fathers of modern football For one of the most influential figures in football history, Lobanovskyi's name is not as well-known as it should be. The modern game simply would not be what it is today without the Ukrainian, who was very much a pioneer in terms of the use of scientific data to analyse matches and opponents. The importance he attached to team work and peak physical condition is also the stuff of legend, with Shevchenko claiming to have seen team-mates begging the coach to call off particularly punishing training sessions. The Ferrari boss pointed to other teams whose drivers managed to race each other without similar consequences: "All the other teams, they were able to overtake each other twenty times during the event. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. This mind-boggling cadence will help the company build out two enormous megaconstellations in low Earth orbit — the next iteration of its Starlink broadband network, which will consist of about 100,000 satellites , and its Starmind AI data-center constellation, which will be 10 times bigger than that . science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998: Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos) Why it mattered As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." science.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
science.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . If you could somehow view the neighborhood from another part of the Milky Way , the familiar arrangement would fall apart. science.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
science.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? Pharaoh Shepseskaf's huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara (Image credit: Jon Bodsworth - www.egyptarchive.co.uk) We know from astronomical calculations that eclipses crossed Egypt long before anyone left an identifiable written record of one. On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. That's where an eclipse almost 1,300 years later becomes particularly intriguing. Is the oldest recorded eclipse hidden in the Bible? Researchers have proposed that an annular eclipse occurred over Canaan on Oct. 30, 1207 BC, and may be described in the Bible. science.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. Alpöge hasn’t published a human-readable version of the proof, saying it would be “obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop'”, though he says an unpublished version ran to more than 250,000 pages. science.description: null A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.
